transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. I'm Dennis. Um, I'm here because I've been having some trouble with my eating. What really made me decide to come in is that... well, once I start eating like that—like, eating a whole lot at once—it feels like I hit some switch. I just keep going, even while part of me is thinking, Dennis, just stop already. I just can't seem to stop myself.
After you eat a large amount like that, do you do anything to try to counteract it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting what you eat afterward?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never tried to make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything like that. I mostly just... sit there feeling really full and bad about myself afterward. But no, I don't try to exercise it off or starve myself the next day to make up for it.
How often would you say these episodes of eating a large amount happen? For example, do they occur multiple times per week, once a week, or less frequently?

I'd say it happens at least once a week, sometimes twice. It really started picking up early in the semester, especially when I have a lot of assignments due or if there's just a bunch of food sitting around the apartment. It's been pretty consistently like that for the last three or four months now.
During these episodes when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you've lost control over how much you're eating, or do you feel like you could stop if you really wanted to?

Yeah, like I was kind of saying earlier, I definitely feel like I completely lose control. I really don't think I could just stop if I wanted to. It really is like a switch flips in my head. I'll be eating and part of me is literally thinking, *Dennis, just stop already*, but... I just keep going anyway. I really can't seem to make myself stop once it starts.
How much does this binge eating bother you or interfere with your life? For example, does it affect your mood, your relationships, your schoolwork, or how you feel about yourself?

It definitely bothers me. I mean, I'm still making it to class and going to my robotics club, so it hasn't completely messed up my schedule or anything. But... I do sometimes feel pretty distracted or just kind of sluggish the next morning. And I definitely spend extra time worrying about whether my roommates noticed what I was doing or how much food is gone. So I guess I'd say it bothers me a lot more than it has actually knocked me off track.

You mentioned you don't make yourself vomit or use laxatives. But I want to make sure I have the complete picture: after these eating episodes, do you ever exercise a lot to try to burn off what you ate, or do you restrict your eating significantly the next day or days after?

No, I don't really do anything like that. I don't go to the gym for hours to work it off, and I don't starve myself the next day either. I just kind of feel bad about it and try to go back to my normal routine, honestly.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to eat less food than usual over the following days to compensate—like eating smaller portions or skipping meals?
No, like I said, I don't really do that either. I don't skip meals or try to eat tiny portions the next day to make up for it. I just go back to eating normally.
